text:
A: Hiya! Graham, is it? I'm Gemma.
B: Hello, duck. Yes, Graham. Can you hear me alright?
A: Yeah, perfect. I've got to say, when I saw your photo you reminded me of my dad. The canal painting and everything. He's always walking the canal.
B: Oh, I'll take that as a compliment, I think. Where are you?
A: Walsall. I walk our dog along the canal most days, and round the Arboretum.
B: Walsall canal. Now that's a proper bit of history, that. All them branches round there used to be packed with boats for the foundries and the leather works.
A: My dad worked in a leather factory! Then he drove a delivery van.
B: There you go. Me dad drove a lorry. And me mum was a dinner lady.
A: No way, so was my mum! She's retired now, but the kids at the school still stop her in Asda.
B: Ha, mine were the same. Couldn't go anywhere. So what do you do, Gemma?
A: Erm, I'm an assistant dog groomer, two days a week, and I'm doing a psychology degree with the Open University. Second year. I want to go into mental health, eventually, if I don't leave it too late.
B: Too late? How old are you, if you don't mind me asking?
A: Thirty-five.
B: No, see, that's not late, that. I'm fifty-eight and I've just started watercolours and Italian. You've got thirty year of work in you yet. And I saw them course books in your picture. That's somebody who means it.
A: Aw, that's really kind. I do worry I'm not clever enough sometimes. My marks are alright though.
B: Well then. Marks don't lie. What are you doing on it at the minute?
A: Erm, a module on anxiety and how people cope with stress, which is sort of close to home, I had a bit of that in my twenties. Sorry, is that too much? I always say too much.
B: Not at all. I had a bad year meself before I packed in engineering. Stress, then me heart started going funny. So I know a bit about it from the wrong end. You'd be good at that job, I reckon. You're easy to talk to.
A: That's two people who've said that today, I'm gonna get big-headed. Are you alright now, with your heart?
B: Oh, it's managed. Tablets, and I walk twenty thousand steps a day on the round. I'm a postie now. Get up at half four.
A: Half four! I'd be useless. My dad won't even go the doctor's, he's terrible. I'm always on at him.
B: Keep on at him. Honestly. I left it far too long, I should've gone months before I did.
A: I'll tell him a postman from Beeston said so. Do you follow football? My dad drags me to Walsall a couple of times a season.
B: Forest, all me life. Walsall, though, I'll give you credit for that, it takes a special kind of suffering.
A: Ha! It does. We have a bacon bap at half time and that's the best bit.
B: A bap? It's a cob, duck.
A: It's a bap! What's a cob?
B: It's a cob. Same thing, round, bread, bacon in it. Saturday morning, there's a new bakery on the High Road does a cracking—
